cards.body:
## Summary
Make every adopt-tier result carry the identity of the bench that produced it, and make the pick compare configs only over cells they all completed, with speed ranked only where every survivor reached an end state.

## Description
The tier bench is resumable and date-keyed: a complete JSON per (scenario, config, rep) is skipped forever. Nothing in the record says which studio prompts, persona/judge prompts, loop cap or scenario sheet produced it, so a resume after a studio change (ADR 0134 records exactly that) splices non-comparable records into one table, and `pick --write` rewrites tiers.json from them. Separately, the pick pools each config's complete records without checking coverage: a config whose hard-band interviews failed is ranked on its easy ones, and its p50 latency includes wall_cap/stalled interviews. The sibling docread bench already pairs units; this card gives adopt_tiers the same discipline in one small module (`cells.py`): a bench digest, the paired cell set, and the conditioned speed view (eval-harness: scenario-design identity + version; outcome-conditioned-cost).

## Flow
- run: each record is stamped `bench_digest`; make_plan re-plans a stale cell and counts it.
- pick/report: load_results drops other-digest records (counted); cells.paired() returns the (scenario, rep) cells every candidate completed; a config under full coverage is disqualified with 'covered k of N cells'; quality aggregates over the paired cells; speed ranks over paired cells where every survivor ended clear|brief; the unconditioned p50 is published beside it with n.
- report.md: a 'Comparability' block (digest, stale excluded, paired n of N).

## Expected impact
A tiers.json write can no longer rest on records from an older studio or on unequal scenario mixes; the operator sees the n behind every pick. Closes the class 'bench resumed across a studio change' and 'config ranked on an easier mix'.

## Evaluation
Claim: the pick is computed over comparable, paired cells of one bench digest.
Before: 0 of 5 new acceptance cases pass (2 guards green by design)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none

cards.body:
## Summary
Turn `pick` from a verdict print into a decision preview: what tiers.json holds now, what the bench proposes, by how much, and refuse to write a pick the floor did not clear unless the operator says so.

## Description
The operator deciding whether to run `pick --write` today sees one line per role and nothing about the incumbent, though both configs' stats are already in memory and tiers.json is one read away. `--write` then writes any pick, fallback included: ADR 0097's first run disqualified every config, and only a hand-confirmation kept a fallback out of the product. This card reverse-maps tiers.json to the bench configs, prints 'incumbent -> proposed' with deltas and n, marks unchanged roles, shows why an incumbent is out, makes an all-unchanged write a no-op, and refuses a fallback write without `--accept-fallback`. Model-routing: policy-governance (approve a diff to routing policy before it applies); measurement-honesty: count-carries-predicate.

## Flow
- `pick`: per role 'opus-low -> haiku-medium: first text -620 ms, accuracy -1.5 pt, judge -0.1, usage -$0.004 (n 18/18)' or 'opus-low (unchanged)'.
- `pick --write`: fallback -> exit 2 naming --accept-fallback; unchanged -> no write.
- report.md pick block: incumbent row beside the proposed row.

## Expected impact
The operator acts on a diff instead of a name; a floor-failing config cannot reach tiers.json by a reflexive --write.

## Evaluation
Claim: pick shows the change against tiers.json and a fallback is not written blind.
Before: 0 of 6 new acceptance cases pass (1 guard green by design)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none
